user.title: Choose the master thermostat
user.description: Pick the thermostat that controls the boiler. Next you choose which of your other thermostats should follow it.

data_description.master_entity: Usually the thermostat that calls for heat from the boiler (for example your Hive thermostat).
data_description.name: Shown as the hub device name in Home Assistant.

rooms.title: Choose the thermostats
rooms.description: Home Assistant knows {count} other thermostat(s). Tick the ones that should follow the master. They are then grouped into rooms by area, and you set up each room in turn — several radiators in one room share one offset and schedule.

room.title: Room: {room}
room.description: Suggested from the area: {thermostats}. Untick a thermostat to leave it for a room of its own; {remaining} thermostat(s) still to place.

data_description.climate_entities: All of them get the room's offset, cut-off and schedule.
data_description.offset: Degrees added to the master target (-2 with a master of 20° gives 18°). Can be changed later with the room's entities.
data_description.off_below: Cut-off: if the room's target (master + offset) would be lower than this, the room is not heated normally — its Off action applies instead (switch off, or frost protection).

abort.already_configured: That thermostat is already set up as a master.

error.no_thermostats: Pick at least one thermostat for this room.
error.name_taken: There is already a room with that name.

user.title: Add rooms
user.description: {count} thermostat(s) aren't in a room yet. Tick the ones to add; they are grouped into rooms by area and you set up each room in turn.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure room
reconfigure.description: Offset and cut-off set here are only used the first time; afterwards adjust them with the room's entities.

data_description.off_below: Cut-off: if the room's target (master + offset) would be lower than this, the room is not heated normally — its Off action applies instead (switch off, or frost protection).

room.title: Room: {room}
room.description: Suggested from the area: {thermostats}. Untick a thermostat to leave it for a room of its own; {remaining} thermostat(s) still to place.

data_description.climate_entities: All of them get the room's offset, cut-off and schedule.
data_description.offset: Degrees added to the master target (-2 with a master of 20° gives 18°). Can be changed later with the room's entities.
data_description.off_below: Cut-off: if the room's target (master + offset) would be lower than this, the room is not heated normally — its Off action applies instead (switch off, or frost protection).

error.no_thermostats: Pick at least one thermostat for this room.
error.name_taken: There is already a room with that name.

abort.no_candidates: Every thermostat Home Assistant knows about is already in a room (or is the master).

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Replace the weekly schedule of a room (or of the master thermostat, when you pick the hub device).

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: The room to schedule, or the hub device to schedule the master thermostat itself (or give the schedule entity instead).

schedule.name: Schedule
schedule.description: Days (mon..sun, or weekdays / weekend / all) mapping to a list of blocks. Each block has a time (HH:MM) and a mode: follow (master + offset; optionally its own offset), fixed (a temperature), or off. A block lasts until the next one starts. The master thermostat accepts only fixed and off.

entity_id.name: Schedule entity
entity_id.description: Alternatively, the room's (or hub's) schedule sensor. Either this or the device is required.

get_schedule.name: Get schedule
get_schedule.description: Return the weekly schedule of a room or of the master thermostat, plus the block currently in effect.

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: The room, or the hub device for the master thermostat (or give the schedule entity instead).

entity_id.name: Schedule entity
entity_id.description: Alternatively, the room's (or hub's) schedule sensor. Either this or the device is required.

clear_schedule.name: Clear schedule
clear_schedule.description: Remove the schedule so the room simply follows the master (or the master is left to its own schedule).

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: The room, or the hub device for the master thermostat (or give the schedule entity instead).

entity_id.name: Schedule entity
entity_id.description: Alternatively, the room's (or hub's) schedule sensor. Either this or the device is required.

sync.name: Sync now
sync.description: Recompute and push targets to the thermostats right away, even if nothing changed. Useful from an automation if a thermostat tends to drift back to its own schedule.

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: Only this room (or this hub). Leave empty to sync everything (or give the schedule entity instead).

entity_id.name: Schedule entity
entity_id.description: Only the room (or hub) this schedule sensor belongs to. Leave both empty to sync everything.

boost.name: Boost
boost.description: Hold the master thermostat (hub device) or a room at a temperature for a while, then go back to the schedule / following. Works with any thermostat, boost function or not.

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: The room to boost, or the hub device for the master thermostat (or give the entity instead).

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: Alternatively, the room's target sensor or the hub's schedule sensor.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Target during the boost. Leave empty for 2° above the current target.

minutes.name: Duration
minutes.description: How long the boost lasts (default 60 minutes).

device_id.name: Room
device_id.description: The room, or the hub device for the master thermostat.

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: Alternatively, the room's target sensor or the hub's schedule sensor.

device_not_found.message: Device {device_id} is not a Cozy Home room or hub.

data_description.enabled: Turn off to stop Cozy Home touching any thermostat (for example over summer). Rooms keep their settings and schedules.
data_description.resync_minutes: Minutes between re-sending each room's target even if nothing changed, for thermostats that drift back to their own schedule. 0 only pushes when something changes.
